title: Admin Pipette: mini-workflows for fast, safe remediation
creator: Leah Zhang
description: Create a small composable 'Pipette' workflow primitive library and runtime integration to let oncall and support surface one-click micro-remediations. Pipette workflows are intentionally tiny (1-5 steps), typed, idempotent, and annotated with safety metadata so they can be executed in dry-run, preview, or live modes. This ticket covers spec, runtime shim in ops-agent, CI/PR gating, and initial rollout via a limited console action set. Goals: reduce mean-time-to-remediate for common incidents without adding blast radius or increasing toil. Non-goals: replace large runbooks or full runbook-as-code DSLs in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Define Pipette manifest schema and safety annotations (inputs, side-effects, required approvals)
Implement runtime executor shim in ops-agent that can run steps in preview, dry-run, and live modes (with noop toggles)
Add telemetry hooks: start/finish/step-success/step-failure, user who executed, approver if required
Console UI surfaces 6 curated Pipette actions for common incidents (service restart, cache flush, scale bump, config toggle, rollout-pin, log-rotate) behind feature gate
All Pipettes pass security review and automated unit/e2e tests; at least two non-production dry-run successful runs recorded in staging
Rollback path documented and automated safety abort if pre-checks fail
design_notes: Pipette manifests are YAML with explicit typed inputs (string/int/enum) and a small step language referencing existing admin APIs and idempotent CLI wrappers
Steps must declare 'read_only' or 'mutating' and optional 'unsafe' flags; mutating steps require either conf file allowlist or 2-step confirm when invoked from console
We will reuse existing KV cache and telemetry event schema from ops-telemetry (avoid duplicating pipelines)
Security: actions that touch secrets must flow a token via ephemeral KMS-wrapped grant; no secret literals in manifests
Execution model: sandbox mode performs API dry-run calls where available; otherwise a simulated mode with expected-diff output
Composability: Pipettes can call other Pipettes only if both are explicitly marked composable to avoid recursion and privilege amplification
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize manifest schema and safety annotation doc; internal design review with SecOps and Oncall (Leah, Priya, Jordan)
Week 2: implement executor shim in ops-agent; provide a local CLI runner for devs with dry-run by default
Week 3: integrate telemetry events and RBAC gating; build console UI skeleton and feature flag
Week 4: create 6 curated Pipettes (staging-tested) and run tabletop with SRE and Support; security review and export manifests to curated repo
Week 5: soft launch to limited team, collect metrics and iterate on safety prompts and required approvals
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser, typed inputs, and safety policy enforcer
E2E tests: staging cluster runs with mocked admin APIs for dry-run and live modes
Chaos test: ensure idempotency when re-running a Pipette after partial failure
Access control test: ensure tokens are required for secret-scoped steps and audit events recorded
Usability test: 3 support engineers run curated Pipettes in staging and provide feedback
monitoring: Telemetry events: pipette.invoked, pipette.step.start, pipette.step.end, pipette.completed, pipette.failed
Dashboards: per-pipette SLOs (success rate, median execution time), operator breakdown, recent dry-run vs live counts
Alerting: >3 failures in 1h for the same pipette triggers review channel and automatic disable of that pipette
Audit trail retention: retain execution records for 180 days in secure audit store
